oneLine: Issues shipping labels and keeps one timeline per package, from handover to delivery, return or loss.

rows.title: Issue a label for a package
rows.story: A vendor asks for a label for one package of a purchase order. The shipping address is fetched live and checked; if it looks like a placeholder the label is refused. Otherwise the label and the package's journey start together.

then.does: adds the tracking number to the booking's expected volume
creates the package row that the order's tracking view reads
keeps the opaque stop id and postal prefix so it can group packages into stops

rows.title: Void a label
rows.story: An operator voids a label that should not be used. It only works while the package is still waiting for pickup; once it is handed over the void is refused.

then.does: marks the package as voided
drops the tracking number from the expected volume; the booking stays

rows.title: Record a scan by hand
rows.story: An operator adds a scan to a package's journey. It follows the same rules as scans from partners: an old, repeated or impossible scan is refused, and a handover or delivery scan also announces that milestone.

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline
judges a handover against the purchase order's ship-by date
records a delivery and judges the promise when it was the last package
records a delivered package; the last one delivers the assignment

rows.title: Note the vendor's shipment confirmation
rows.story: The vendor says a shipment has left. Each package on it gets a 'shipment confirmed' scan, but its journey does not move: the handover waits for the carrier's pickup.
rows.policy: Whenever a vendor confirms a shipment, add one scan per tracking number

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Hand the package over at pickup
rows.story: A load leaves its origin. The first pickup departure of a labelled package hands it over to the carrier; any later departure is just a movement.
rows.policy: Whenever a load departs, add one scan per package; the first pickup hands it over

then.does: judges the handover against the purchase order's ship-by date
adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Follow the package through the middle mile
rows.story: A load arrives. At a delivery station the package becomes ready to go out; at any other hub it stays in transit.
rows.policy: Whenever a load arrives, add one scan per package: station arrival or transit arrival

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Show the package out for delivery
rows.story: The delivery station sends the package out on a route. The journey moves to out for delivery.
rows.policy: Whenever a package goes out for delivery, add an out-for-delivery scan

then.does: adds the scan to the order's tracking timeline

rows.title: Close the journey on delivery
rows.story: A delivery attempt ends. A successful one delivers the package and closes the journey; a failed one sends it back to the station and the journey stays open.
rows.policy: Whenever an attempt is made, add a delivered or failed scan to the journey

then.does: records the delivery and judges the promise when it was the last package
records a delivered package; the last one delivers the assignment
marks the package and its order group delivered

rows.title: Return a package to the sender
rows.story: After repeated failed attempts, last-mile-delivery starts a return. A package waiting at the station becomes returned, which ends its journey.
rows.policy: Whenever a return is started, mark the package at the station as returned

then.does: records the return and judges the promise broken
marks the package and its order group returned
refunds the order, or waits until its payment exists

rows.title: Store the day-of delivery window
rows.story: When a route starts, last-mile-delivery gives each stop a time window. Every package of the stop keeps it; the window shows only while the package is out for delivery.
rows.policy: Whenever a stop gets a time window, store it on each package of the stop

then.does: keeps the window for the order's tracking view unless a newer one exists

rows.title: Relay a delivery-point warning
rows.story: last-mile-delivery flags a delivery point after two failed attempts. It knows the stop, not the order, so this context passes the warning on for each package of the stop, without any address.
rows.policy: Whenever a delivery point is flagged, store the flag on each open package of the stop

then.does: keeps the flag on the package's tracking view so the shopper can be advised

rows.title: Raise an exception on silence
rows.story: A periodic sweep looks for open packages with no new scan for longer than their service tier allows. Each silent package gets one exception until a new scan arrives.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any package silent past its window raises one exception

then.does: treats the exception as a risk to the promise and may re-promise
records the exception on the order's tracking view

rows.title: Declare a silent package lost
rows.story: If a package in transit stays silent for 48 hours after its exception, the same sweep declares it lost and closes its journey.
rows.policy: Every sweep, an in-transit package with an unanswered exception for 48 hours is lost

then.does: records the loss and judges the promise broken
marks the package and its order group lost
refunds the order, or waits until its payment exists

rows.title: Keep the product dimensions copy
rows.story: Every product that offer-availability creates leaves its size, weight and handling flags here. Nothing reads them yet.
rows.policy: Whenever a catalogue item is created, store its dimensions and handling flags

rows.title: Delete old delivery addresses
rows.story: The saved, encrypted delivery address is deleted 30 days after its journey closes, whether delivered, returned, lost or voided.
rows.policy: Every housekeeping run, delete addresses of journeys closed over 30 days ago

hotspots.text: Voiding a label and recording a scan by hand have no named caller: the routes are unauthenticated and the contracts name nobody.
A placeholder-looking address refuses the label, but no loop asks the shopper to fix it. That is deliberately left out.
News about a package this context never labelled is counted and dropped. Nothing keeps it for a later look.
A delivery-point warning is never cleared by an event. It ends only when the package's journey ends.
A restricted route through which partners could resolve the delivery address is not built.

opportunities.text: The product dimensions copy has no reader yet. It is kept so a printable label can use it later.
